review_evidence: README states that the repository contains Lean 4 and Isabelle/HOL solutions to the Calculemus formal-mathematics exercises and indexes the exercises by theorem/topic and date.

All 312 current-primary files are Lean source files, with filenames and README entries covering algebra, order theory, set theory, logic, analysis, sequences, number theory, functions, equivalence relations, and combinatorics.

The primary surface is therefore the exercise proof corpus itself rather than surrounding prose/build metadata; no source-local hard-exclusion class was established without discarding formal statements or alternative proofs useful for retrieval.
summary: Retain all 312 primary Calculemus2 Lean exercise formalizations as mathematical statement/proof prior art.

review_evidence: Ran `grep -cE '\b(theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom)\b'` over all 17 files; every file had a nonzero match count (range 4-20).

Read src/5²ⁿ_-_2³ⁿ_es_divisible_por_17.lean in full (14997 bytes, 468 lines, the largest file in the unit): an induction proof that 17 divides 5^(2n) - 2^(3n), given first as a natural-language proof then as multiple Lean `example` proofs with step-by-step comments.

Read src/No_converge_a_límite_pequeño_si_infinitos_términos_grandes.lean in full (4091 bytes, 109 lines): a natural-language proof sketch, a `LimSuc` definition, three alternative Lean proofs of the same non-convergence statement, and a closing block of `#check`-cited lemmas used.
summary: Ran the declaration-keyword grep across all 17 changed/added exercise files: every file had nonzero matches (range 4-20), so no zero-content candidate exists. Read the largest file in full and the smallest file in full as representative samples of this source's exercise-solution format. Both follow the source's established pattern: a natural-language proof sketch as a header comment, followed by one or more Lean `example`/proof blocks (often several alternative proofs of the same statement), and a closing block of `#check` lemma citations. Consistent with the prior review's characterization of this source as 312 mathematical statement/proof exercise formalizations. All 17 files stay searchable; no exclusions.
